data.name: Klang
data.detailed_description:
Klang é uma abordagem inovadora aos tradicionais jogos de ritmo que leva o género para lá do simples premir de botões no tempo certo, levando-te até um mundo de exploração acelerada, plataformas e combate.

No Klang, os jogadores assumem o papel de um guerreiro rave de elite, que com a sua espada afinada tentará libertar-se das correntes do Senhor do Som Sonus. Funde-te com a música à medida que lutas para passar níveis cada vez mais desafiantes, sincronizando cada ação e ataque com as deixas audiovisuais.

Com a energia musical do lendário compositor de música eletrónica, bLiNd, Klang é um rasgo de adrenalina capaz de desafiar até os mais habituados a conciliar várias atividades ao mesmo tempo.

Principais características

  • Jogabilidade rápida e eufórica baseada em ritmos
  • Visual néon magnífico
  • Banda sonora original criada pelo famoso compositor de música eletrónica, bLiNd
  • 2 a 4 horas de jogo, mais um modo de dificuldade Nightcore para separar quem é verdadeiramente hardcore de todos os outros
  • Joga com um teclado, comando da Xbox 360, Xbox One ou PS4

reviews.review:
Klang is an inventive fusion of rhythm gaming, precision platforming, and fast-paced action that refuses to settle for the traditional formula of simply pressing buttons in time with music. Developed by Tinimations and published by Snow Cannon Games, it places players in control of a tuneblade-wielding rave warrior fighting to escape the influence of Soundlord Sonus. The premise is intentionally straightforward, allowing the game to concentrate on its strongest feature: turning an electronic soundtrack into an interactive obstacle course where movement, combat, and timing become interconnected.

The gameplay is where Klang establishes its identity. Instead of separating platforming from musical sequences, the game expects players to perform both simultaneously. Running through stages, avoiding hazards, positioning the character, and responding to attacks can all depend on recognizing audiovisual cues. It creates a demanding form of multitasking where listening to the music becomes almost as important as watching the screen. Once the mechanics begin to click, successful sequences have a wonderful sense of flow, making it feel as though the player is actively participating in the soundtrack rather than merely hearing it in the background.

Combat follows the same rhythm-driven philosophy. Attacks and defensive responses must be performed with accurate timing, while the player continues dealing with environmental challenges. This combination can initially feel overwhelming because Klang frequently demands attention in several directions at once. The difficulty steadily increases, forcing players to develop muscle memory and become comfortable reading its visual language. Mistakes can be frustrating, particularly during complicated sequences, but improvement is noticeable as previously intimidating patterns gradually become manageable.

The soundtrack is easily one of the game's greatest strengths. Music from EDM composer bLiNd gives the adventure an aggressive electronic pulse that fits perfectly with its futuristic rave atmosphere. Tracks are not simply decorative additions to each level. Their rhythms help dictate the structure and pace of encounters, creating a strong connection between sound and mechanical design. Playing with headphones makes the synchronization especially enjoyable because individual beats and cues become easier to recognize while also increasing the intensity of the overall experience.

Its presentation complements the music extremely well. Klang uses a colorful 2D visual style dominated by neon lighting, futuristic environments, sharp contrasts, and effects that react naturally to the energetic soundtrack. At its best, the combination of music, movement, and animation creates the impression of controlling an elaborate electronic music video. The downside is that the screen can occasionally become visually busy. Players already concentrating on platforming and rhythmic prompts may find some moments difficult to process, especially when multiple effects and hazards appear together.

Klang is relatively compact, with the primary experience designed around approximately two to four hours of gameplay. That makes it noticeably shorter than many platformers, but the limited duration also prevents its central mechanic from becoming excessively repetitive. Players who enjoy mastering rhythm games can extract considerably more value by replaying stages, pursuing Steam achievements, and tackling the unlockable Nightcore difficulty. This harder mode provides an appropriate additional challenge for anyone who finishes the standard experience and wants something considerably more demanding.

Controller support is another welcome aspect of the PC release. The game was designed to accommodate keyboard controls along with common controllers, and a gamepad feels particularly natural for its combination of movement and rhythmic reactions. The mechanical requirements are not complicated individually, but the challenge comes from performing them accurately while processing the soundtrack and environmental hazards. This makes Klang relatively easy to understand while still leaving plenty of room for mastery.

Steam Deck compatibility requires more caution. Klang does not have an official Steam Deck compatibility rating displayed for the game, so its status should be considered Unknown or Unverified rather than officially Verified or Playable. The Steam release is officially configured for Windows, meaning Steam Deck users may need to rely on Proton compatibility. Its full controller support and relatively modest hardware demands are encouraging characteristics for handheld experimentation, but they should not be mistaken for an official guarantee of flawless Steam Deck operation.

The game also shows its age in a few areas. Its presentation remains stylish, but the underlying package is relatively small, and players looking for a deep campaign, extensive progression system, large collection of modes, or lengthy narrative will not find those things here. Klang is much more focused on delivering a short and intense rhythm-platforming experience. That narrow focus is simultaneously one of its biggest limitations and one of its greatest strengths. There is very little unnecessary material standing between the player and the core action.

Overall, Klang remains an unusual and memorable rhythm game because it treats music as an essential component of movement and combat rather than merely a timing track. The energetic soundtrack, neon presentation, challenging multitasking, and satisfying synchronization give it a personality that distinguishes it from conventional rhythm titles. Its short length and demanding presentation will not appeal equally to everyone, but players who enjoy electronic music, precision challenges, and unconventional genre combinations should find a surprisingly engaging experience. When its music, platforming, and combat align perfectly, Klang delivers an exhilarating sense of rhythm that few games approach in quite the same way.

Rating: 8/10

pc_requirements.minimum:
Mínimos:
  • Requer um sistema operativo e processador de 64 bits
  • Sistema Operativo *: Windows 7
  • Processador: Intel Core i7-2670QM 2.2GHz
  • Memória: 4 GB de RAM
  • Placa gráfica: GeForce GT 630M
  • DirectX: Versão 10
  • Espaço no disco: Requer 2 GB de espaço livre
  • Notas adicionais: Because Klang is a 2D game, some laptops will default to running it off of their integrated GPUs. If you plan on playing Klang on a laptop, we recommend that you run the game off of your dedicated gaming GPU. (NOTE: If Klang detects that your laptop is using its integrated GPU, instructions for how to switch to your dedicated GPU will be provided in game.)
pc_requirements.recommended:
Recomendados:
  • Requer um sistema operativo e processador de 64 bits
  • Placa gráfica: GeForce GTX 580
  • Notas adicionais: For an optimal gameplay experience, we recommend playing Klang on desktop computers with PC monitors.
